topic: Odd modular squares at powers of two: exception-sensitive criterion retrieval

cognitive.X: Identify the necessary and sufficient condition that distinguishes an odd square residue modulo 2^k; note the exceptional small exponent.
cognitive.Y: Previously reconstructed odd-square residues modulo 8 and basic reduction of squares modulo small powers of two.
cognitive.Z: Select the correct classification criterion for k>=3 instead of overgeneralizing oddness or the modulo4 case.
cognitive.W: Independently retrieve the correct threshold-specific criterion a≡1 (mod8) for k>=3, classify unfamiliar residues, and switch criterion at k=2.
cognitive.wrong_idea: Every odd residue is a square, or residue 1 modulo4 is enough for every power of two.
cognitive.replacement_rule: For odd a and k>=3, odd square roots modulo 2^k exist exactly when a≡1 (mod8); for k=2 the exact criterion is a≡1 (mod4).

difficulty_proposal.basis: High-transfer exceptional exponent boundary rather than many calculations; D4 provisional because criterion selection at k=2 versus k>=3 must remain learner-owned.
difficulty_proposal.adjacent_D3_alternative: A familiar single gcd/modular arithmetic procedure or a supplied rule followed stepwise would be D2/D3, not D4. A qualified reviewer must confirm whether the exceptional criterion is genuinely novel and instructionally fair.

core2a.prompt: An odd residue a modulo 128 is called an odd-square residue if some odd integer x satisfies x²≡a (mod128). Without listing all 128 possibilities, classify a=9,13,17,21,33,49. Name the exact defining criterion and give one counterexample to 'all odd residues work'.
givens: All six candidate residues are odd.
Classification, not finding individual square roots, is the primary requested answer.

expected.criterion: Odd a modulo 2^k for k>=3 is an odd-square residue iff a≡1 mod8.

core2a.H1: Which property must a candidate residue have to be the square of an odd integer? Avoid computing six roots.
core2a.H2: Use a short odd-square example at a lower power of two as an anchor; ask whether every power of two has the same boundary.
core2a.H3_after_nonblank: Odd squares are 1 modulo8, and every odd class congruent 1 modulo8 lifts to a square at higher powers of two. Distinguish k>=3 from the k=2 exception.
core2a.math_proof: For necessity, (2t+1)^2=4t(t+1)+1≡1 mod8. For sufficiency, modulo8 every residue 1 mod8 has a root; if x²≡a modulo2^k, replacing odd x by x+2^(k−1) flips the k-th binary bit of the square modulo2^(k+1) (k>=3), allowing a lift to either residue. Hence induction.

core2b.changed_task: The modulus is now 4 instead of 128; classify odd residues a=5,9,13 and contrast the result for a=5 modulo8.
core2b.correct_answer: All 5,9,13 are 1 modulo4 and have odd square roots modulo4. The residue 5 has no root modulo8; the small-modulus exception is genuine.
core2b.different_W: Retrieve and switch to the k=2 criterion; do not reuse 1 mod8 from the earlier problem.

role_plans.CORE1: Orient parity, modular equivalence and difference between being an integer square and a square residue; do not publish the main six classifications.
role_plans.CORE1A: Build odd-square residues on a different, small modulo8 anchor (for instance 1,3,5,7) and make the student independently classify a new modulo16 near-neighbor with an after-teaching exit.
role_plans.CORE1B: Misconception: odd implies square or mod4 criterion automatically applies at k>=3. Boundary: 5 is 1 modulo4 but not a square modulo8; ask for the corrected defining condition.
role_plans.CORE2A: Classify six nonconsecutive odd residues modulo128; learners must retrieve the threshold condition, not brute-force calculate roots; H3 after nonblank attempt only.
role_plans.CORE2B: Changed modulus4 classification of 5/9/13 and counterexample modulo8, independently asking for correct boundary condition.

independent_oracle.method: Enumerate odd x and all odd residue classes modulo 2^k for k=2..10 and compare to the proposed criterion
